newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel probes dumping of German polyethylene.
newsitem.headline: Israel probes dumping of German polyethylene.

text.p: Israel's Industry and Trade Ministry said on Sunday it is investigating whether a German company is dumping recycled polyethylene on the Israeli market.

The ministry said it launched the inquiry after Amnir Recycling Ltd, a subsidiary of American Israeli Paper Mills, complained that the German company Rethmann Plano was receiving a 15 percent subsidy to manufacture the material.
"This subsidy, according to Amnir, allows the German manufacturer to sell his supply at dumping prices," the ministry said in a statement.

An attorney for the ministry said countervailing duties could not be imposed on the polyethylene because the subsidy was being provided by a private German group -- as an incentive for companies to recycle polyethylene -- and not by the government.
"If the government was providing the subsidy, we could impose duties according to international regulations," said attorney Levy Elad.
"But since this is a private group, it poses a problem," he told Reuters.
But Eli Weinberg, Alumnir's managing director, said he believed that the government could still impose the duties because the subsidy is being made as part of a government-sponsored initiative.
Elad said the German company's low prices were driving down market prices in Israel and making it difficult for Israeli companies to compete.
